segments.text: We yawn because we need more oxygen. Well, that's not exactly true. When scientists gave people extra oxygen, they kept yawning just the same.
One leading idea is that yawning cools your brain. A big gulp of air and a long stretch of the jaw bring fresh blood up to your head.
Here's the wild part. Babies start yawning before they're even born, while they're still inside the womb.
In fact, yawns are contagious. Just seeing someone yawn, or even reading about it, can set you off.
And you're more likely to catch a yawn from people you're close to, like family and friends.
That's not all. Dogs can catch yawns from their humans too.
So, did you yawn while watching this? Tell me in the comments.
